title: fails on an id the triage does not cover, and names it
why: An id the triage has never seen passed over: OSV's new matches would never turn the weekly run red, which is the only notification there is.

title: fails on an open id past its due date, and not on the day it is due
why: The due date ignored: an open id stays green for ever, and the fix budget is a number nobody is held to.

title: never calls a network failure clean
why: A run that never reached OSV exits as a clean one: the week OSV is down is the week nothing is watched, and the run says all is well.

title: never calls a network failure clean
why: An HTTP error read as an answer: a 503 whose body happens to parse would be judged as OSV's word on the components.

title: never calls a network failure clean
why: A short answer taken whole: the queries OSV did not answer would read as components with no vulnerability.

title: fails on a triaged id OSV no longer returns, and says to take it out
why: A triaged id OSV has stopped returning goes unmentioned, so the triage keeps entries for fixes that have shipped and nobody is told to take them out.

title: takes an id triaged at another version as untriaged
why: A verdict read against one version kept after the pin moves: a not-reachable judged on 3.12.14 would stand for whatever the runtime becomes.

title: takes an id OSV now rates otherwise as untriaged
why: A re-rated id kept at its old rating: a medium raised to critical would keep its 60 days instead of 14.

find: if (!('due' in entry)) say('is open and has no "due" date')
title: refuses an open entry with no due date, and a closed one with one
why: An open entry with no due date accepted: it can never be overdue, so the budget never applies to it.

title: refuses a due date past the budget for its severity
why: A due date written past the budget accepted: a critical reachable id could be given a year.

title: builds one query per component from the pins, sharing one for two pins that ask the same
why: CPython asked about by its version rather than its tag: OSV's GIT records list tags, so the query matches nothing and the runtime's twenty-odd ids vanish from the watch.

title: refuses pins that name a component the watch does not read, or lack a field it reads
why: A component added to the pins without a query is let through, and the installers carry something the watch never asks about.

title: follows OSV's pages, and asks again only for the query that has another
why: Only OSV's first page read: a component with more ids than a page holds is judged on part of them.

title: refuses a key the pins gain inside a component the watch reads
why: Only the top level of the pins checked: a library added as ffmpeg.libvpx, loom_windows_static.libpng or python.openssl ships unwatched, and the run stays green.

title: watches the Windows runtime's zlib at the version its licence record names
why: The Windows runtime's zlib left to coincidence: while it shares FFmpeg's version it is watched by accident, and the day python-build-standalone moves it, nothing asks about it.

title: refuses a requirements line it cannot read as a pin
why: A requirements line in another form skipped in silence: a package pinned with >= or a URL drops out of the watch while the lock still ships it.

title: takes an id returned for two components as untriaged unless each has its entry
why: One component of an id judged for all: an id triaged for zlib and returned for CPython too passes on the zlib entry, and the CPython reading is never made.

title: takes an id the triage rates below the CVE record, with no note saying why, as untriaged
why: A rating below the CVE record accepted without a word: a critical written as medium takes 60 days instead of 14, and nothing says it was a choice.

find: if (cve !== null && (given === null || given.startsWith('CVSS:'))) rateFrom.set(id, cve)
title: takes an id the triage rates below the CVE record, with no note saying why, as untriaged
why: The CVE record never read: the rating the triage gives a vector is checked against nothing.

title: never takes an answer that drops every id of a triaged component for a clean one
why: An answer with every id of a component gone taken as a fix: a broken OSV, or a change in how it matches a GIT tag, turns the run green with the triage moved to "no longer returned".

title: never takes an answer whose canaries are silent for a clean one
why: A silent canary ignored: OSV stops matching PyPI versions, the packages, which the triage holds nothing for, read as clean, and the run is green.

title: gives each request its own time limit, against a fetch that never answers
why: No limit per request: one wedged request holds the whole run until its deadline, and every request after it gets nothing.

title: gives each request its own time limit, against a fetch that never answers
why: The limit left to the fetch honouring its signal: a request that ignores the abort hangs the run past every limit, and the job is cancelled with nothing said.

title: stops at its own deadline, inside the workflow job's timeout
why: No deadline for the run: twenty slow pages and a record each outlast the job's ten minutes, and GitHub cancels it with no summary and no exit status of the watch's own.

title: fails on a triaged id OSV no longer returns, and says to take it out
why: A triaged id OSV stops returning passed over: an answer missing one of CPython's twenty-odd ids, with the canaries answering, exits 0 and calls clean what it could not vouch for.

find: if (cve !== null && (given === null || given.startsWith('CVSS:'))) rateFrom.set(id, cve)
title: holds an id OSV gives no severity to the rating of its CVE alias
why: An id OSV gives no severity never read against its CVE alias: were OSV to return only the PSF's id for a critical CVE, it would sit at unrated with 60 days instead of 14.

title: holds an id OSV gives no severity to the rating of its CVE alias
why: The alias read and its rating thrown away: the same 60 days for a critical.

find: const rule = Object.hasOwn(shape, key) ? shape[key] : shape[ANY]
replace: const rule = Object.hasOwn(shape, key) ? shape[key] : KNOWN
title: refuses a library a target's licence record or configure line gains
why: The per-target maps taken whole: a library a target's licence record gains, LICENSE.openssl-3.txt with its version, ships unwatched and unrefused.

title: refuses a library a target's licence record or configure line gains
why: FFmpeg's configure lines unread: a build that adds --enable-libdav1d ships a library no query asks about.

title: watches the Windows runtime's zlib at the version its licence record names
why: A zlib licence record that names no version skipped as though it were absent: the runtime's zlib drops out of the watch the day the record changes shape.

title: refuses an id it would not put in a URL
why: An id taken as OSV wrote it into the URL of the record read next: '../x' reads another path of the API than the record asked for.

title: takes a CVE id only when it is one, whole
why: An alias that only contains a CVE id taken for one: 'CVE-2026-12345/../../x' goes into the CVE service's URL as written.

title: counts a sentence that begins with a name in lower case
why: A sentence that begins with 'requests' or 'pandas' not counted: a reason of four sentences passes as three.
